objective: The `items` command in `stockroom/cli.py` measures its columns and pads every cell by hand with `ljust` and `rjust`, while the rest of the package pads text through `textutil.align`. Move the catalogue listing out of the command into a function `items_table(items, symbol="$")` in `stockroom/report.py` that returns the listing as text, make the command print it, and route all space padding through `textutil.align`. This is a pure refactor: the listing printed by `stockroom items` stays byte for byte the same for every catalogue, and the existing tests keep passing without being edited.
acceptance: `report.items_table(items, symbol)` returns the catalogue listing without a trailing newline, with the layout the `items` command printed before: columns `SKU`, `Name`, `Price` separated by two spaces; each column as wide as its widest cell or its header; the header line left-aligned in every column; then a rule of `-` per column width; then one line per item in the given order with SKU and name left-aligned and the price (formatted with the currency symbol) right-aligned; trailing spaces removed from every line; an empty catalogue gives the header line and the rule only
The `symbol` argument defaults to `$`, and no line of the result ends with a space
`stockroom items --file F [--tag T]` (run through `cli.main`) exits 0, prints the listing of `items_table` followed by one newline, nothing on stderr, and honours the currency symbol setting
Outside `textutil.align`, no module of the `stockroom` package and no script pads text with spaces by calling `ljust`, `rjust` or `center` with a single argument
`textutil.align` itself is unchanged for `left`, `right`, `center`, a width smaller than the text, and an unknown alignment name (which raises `ValueError`)
